title: cplane-field-sprint-viz-notes-2026-04-19
content:
Context:
This was an ad-hoc field sprint sync focused on landing a lightweight control-plane visualizer (prototype) to help SREs and oncall quickly diagnose routing/auth/quotas fallthroughs. Notes are rough — capture of a 40m workshop + standup fragments.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (notes / facilitator)
- Jonas Becker (routing owner)
- Ruth Hernandez (auth & policy)
- Ali Noor (quota systems)
- Samir Patel (SRE, shadow)
- Heather Lowe (UX consult, 20m)

Goal for the sprint:
- Ship a small, read-only viz that shows per-route recent decision path (route -> auth -> quota -> backend) for the last 100 requests in a 5m window.
- Provide clear low-effort drill-down links to logs / spans / token-level cost.
- Validate that the viz helps debug: 1) quota fallthroughs, 2) auth denies causing routing backfills, 3) model variant fallbacks.

Quick wins (agreed):
- Jonas will export the existing routing decision trace from the controlplane debug API as a compact JSON (schema v1) and put it at /internal/viz/sample for the prototype. (owner: Jonas, due: 2026-04-21) [JIRA-ENG-2314] 
- Ruth to supply a redacted example of an auth deny + policy evaluation trace that includes policy id & reason codes. (owner: Ruth, due: 2026-04-20)
- Ali to expose quota counters per-client with a small TTL cache endpoint that the viz can query without hitting main quota DB. (owner: Ali, due: 2026-04-23)

Design constraints raised by UX (Heather):
- Minimal state: viz should default to streaming last-N events; no long-term storage for now.
- Color/affordance for a chain: green = allowed, amber = throttled/fallback, red = deny.
- We need a compact breadcrumb row for each request: [route] - [auth:ok/deny] - [quota:ok/burst] - [backend:variantX/fallbackY] - [latency ms].

Prototype plan (MVP):
1) Backends: controlplane debug API + small quota cache endpoint + link to traces (trace id).
2) Frontend: single static page in controlplane repo, no auth for internal only (dev env). Use simple list + expand details per event.
3) Metrics: add a tiny counter for "viz_loads" and "viz_sample_size" to gauge usage.

Risks / open questions:
- Data privacy: some traces include customer ids; need to decide redaction policy for demo data. (Ruth + privacy team?)
- Performance: streaming full traces could cost CPU if used in prod — need rate limit. Proposed: 1 request/sec per user, cached 5s. (owner: Maya to add to implementation notes)
- Backfill behavior: should viz show synthetic backfills? For now, show only actual request traces. Consider an "include-backfill" toggle later.

Hand-off items & owners:
- Jonas: produce sample JSON schema + small Node script to emit sanitized sample file (JIRA-ENG-2314). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/289. (ETA 2026-04-21)
- Ruth: privacy redaction checklist + example deny traces. (ETA 2026-04-20)
- Ali: quota cache endpoint + notes on cardinality. (ETA 2026-04-23)
- Maya: wireframe + list of queries for the viz, write README in repo (ETA 2026-04-22)
- Samir: schedule a 30m playtest on 2026-04-26 with oncall rotation to get feedback. (ETA invite: Maya)

Standup snippets (quick status from each):
- Jonas: "routing exporter mostly done, need to add route meta (tier, fallback policy id)."
- Ruth: "policy engine minor change: add reason_code to evaluation result; will require small schema bump."
- Ali: "quota cache prototype in local testing, some flakiness with client key normalization."
- Samir: "Can we include recent error-percent in each event row? helps triage."

Quick priority list (this sprint):
1) schema + sanitized sample JSON (blocker for frontend dev)
2) quota cache endpoint and auth traces
3) frontend skeleton and UX review
4) internal playtest and iterate

Notes-to-self / rough commands:
- To get routing traces locally: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer dev-token' https://controlplane-internal.dev/v1/debug/traces?limit=100 > sample.json
- Sanitize script: scripts/sanitize_traces.py --strip-customer --map-ip-to-mask sample.json > sample.sanitized.json

Small decisions made during meeting:
- No persisted storage for traces in MVP; all views derive from in-memory window sampling. (pros: no infra; cons: transient)
- Use trace_id as canonical drill-down key; link to existing tracing UI for spans.
- Color semantics: DENY = red, FALLBACK/THROTTLE = amber, OK = green.

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Quick sync on 2026-04-22 11:00 (30m) to validate Jonas's sample + Ruth's redaction output; calendar invite out.
- Playtest with oncall: 2026-04-26 09:30.

Misc thoughts / brainstorm (scratchpad):
- Could eventually add a heatmap view: routes on Y, time on X, color by error-rate / fallback-rate.
- Consider tagging events with "cost-per-request" bucket to spot expensive fallbacks.
- If the sampler proves useful, think about a small retention store (30d) behind an admin toggle.

Appendix: Example compact event (proto):
- id: 6f2e1a
- ts: 2026-04-19T15:03:12Z
- route: /v1/generate (tier: prod, route_id: R-211)
- auth: {result: ALLOW, policy_id: P-83}
- quota: {result: THROTTLE, bucket: client:12345, remaining: 0}
- backend: {served_variant: tiny-quant, fallback: small-ptx}
- latency_ms: 142
- trace_id: trace-000123

(That's it — will flesh README + quickstart once sample schema lands.)

-- Maya
